newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb wounds two in Algerian capital.
newsitem.headline: Bomb wounds two in Algerian capital.

text.p: A parcel bomb exploded on Saturday in the centre of the Algerian capital Algiers, wounding two people, Algerian security services said.
The attack, the fourth in three days, occurred midway through campaigning for the June 5 parliamentary election.
The bomb went off at 11.25 a.m. in Asselah Hocine Street, a statement carried by the official Algerian news agency APS said.
Two car bombs killed seven people and wounded 12 in the western town of Tlemcen on Friday, and at least 12 people were killed on Thursday when a car bomb rocked the town of Boufarik south of Algiers.
About 60,000 people have been killed in violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
